_field_contract: resume.sh does os.path.isdir(worktree) and git rev-list origin/<branch>..HEAD, so `worktree` and `branch` must each be ONE value. _ci: CI RAN FOR THE FIRST TIME IN THIS PROGRAM, and this is the record of what that cost and bought. pr-validation.yml triggered ONLY on `pull_request: branches: [main]`, and the program is forbidden from opening a PR until final integration - so sixty landed items, twelve landings and ~2000 Rust tests had been verified on exactly one laptop. `gh run list --branch roadmap/v2.2` returned nothing at all. Fixed in four commits, each one exposing the next problem: (1) push + workflow_dispatch triggers added; the first run failed in 18s. (2) The parity check cloned apex-shell's DEFAULT branch, so it compared apex-os roadmap/v2.2 against apex-shell main and reported drift on two touchpad defaults - while the two INTEGRATION branches agreed perfectly at 22 settings. It now clones the matching branch and PRINTS which one it used. THE DRIFT IT EXPOSED IS REAL AND IS KEPT: apex-shell main has drag_lock=true and click_method=clickfinger where apex-os main's generator has false and buttonAreas, so whoever does the final integration must land both sides together or opening the Input page silently changes a user's touchpad behaviour. (3) The path classifier read github.event.pull_request.* and died with exit 128 on a push; it is now event-aware and, when no range can be determined, selects EVERYTHING - this file already records four occasions where a selector picked nothing, the job skipped, and the workflow passed. (4) Six confinement assertions in mcp_sidecar_live.rs had never run anywhere but the L16 because the runner has no bubblewrap; installed rather than skipped, because they are the assertions that the sandbox IS a sandbox. Then bwrap failed on Ubuntu 24.04's kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1, so the sysctl is relaxed and PROVEN with a smoke check before any test runs. THE FINDING THAT PAYS FOR ALL OF IT: on the runner, /proc/N/cgroup reads '/system.slice/hosted-compute-agent.service', which is neither a login session nor a user service - a THIRD classification distinct from the L16's session scope and from scheduled-job. Two request_origin tests fail there while nine pass. Four rounds of orchestrators wrote that the workflow file was the only evidence of what CI presents; it is now measured, and p0-014 has been sent the exact string while it is still live.
